system.name: Databricks Genie
system.version: Genie conversations API (Space grounded on the 22 base tables), databricks-sdk 0.136.0

declarations.artifacts: databricks_agent/captures/genie_captures_run{1,2,3}.jsonl (149 single-turn) and genie_captures_mt_run{1,2,3}.jsonl (41 multi-turn turns), concatenated to genie_captures_190_run{1,2,3}.jsonl. Each row carries the question, Genie's SQL, the returned columns/types/rows, latency, conversation_id and the timeout in force. runs/genie_answer_run{1,2,3}.jsonl are the decoded answers, runs/genie_answer_sub{1,2,3}.json the submissions, runs/genie_answer_3run_score/ the verdicts.
declarations.notes: COMMERCIAL BAND: Genie is a managed product bringing its own undisclosed model, so this is NOT a scaffold comparison against the four controlled arms, which all run gpt-5.6-luna. It belongs with Claude Code and Snowflake Cortex Analyst. ANSWER-TRACK, AND THIS ROW IS THE BOARD'S ONE EXCEPTION: every other arm is SQL-track -- the harness re-executes the agent's SQL on the single reference warehouse. This row is scored on the rows GENIE'S OWN warehouse returned, with nothing re-executed. That is only valid if the Databricks tables hold the data gold was computed from, so it was proved before any metered call: all 22 tables present, every row count exact (58,463,766 total), every column set matching, and 1,238 per-column aggregates (COUNT, COUNT DISTINCT, SUM, MIN, MAX) identical on both engines. The SQL-track was then computed from the SAME captures as a cross-check and lands at 115/190 against answer-track's 117/190 -- a 2-task, 1.1pp difference, which is the evidence that the load is faithful and the two methods agree. The SQL-track figure required adding one dialect rule (try_divide, which DuckDB lacks); before it, 63 statements that ran correctly on Databricks failed on DuckDB, and the cross-check would have measured the shim's coverage rather than the agent. DECODING: the Databricks SQL API returns every cell as a string, so values are decoded to native types using the column types Databricks reported in the same response. Nothing is rounded, reinterpreted or repaired; a cell that will not decode is left verbatim and allowed to fail. An executed query returning zero rows is submitted as the empty set, not as a missing answer -- 9 of the 10 tier-7 negative controls have the empty set as gold, and conflating the two would fail them. MULTI-TURN IS CHAINED THROUGH GENIE'S OWN CONVERSATION: turn 1 opens a conversation and every later turn is sent to that same conversation_id, so the agent carries its own context exactly as a user would experience it. No authored gold prior is ever substituted. Threading was verified intact across all 24 captured sessions. TIME LIMIT: 180 s per question, passed explicitly into the SDK and recorded on every row. This matters -- databricks-sdk's *_and_wait helpers default to a 1200 s timeout, so an unset value would have given Genie 6.7x the budget every other arm runs under. CAPTURE HEALTH: 570/570 executions recorded with status ok, zero retries, zero truncation, zero auth failures, zero rate-limit backoffs; 570/570 produced SQL. RE-CAPTURE DISCLOSED: in the first pass, four turns of one 9-turn session timed out when the capture host entered macOS Maintenance Sleep mid-call (confirmed by pmset, and by wall-clock elapsed exceeding measured latency by 14-53 minutes while time.monotonic stalled). Those were not Genie failures. That whole session was discarded and re-captured as a single clean conversation with sleep inhibited; the re-capture moved Pass^3 from 115 to 117 and tier-8 from 17 to 19. No other execution in the run was affected. ROW CAP: stored result rows are capped at 100,000, matching the Snowflake arm. An earlier 1,000 cap sat below the largest gold answer in the corpus (1,322 rows, Set-Match) and would have truncated and failed that task while uncapped arms got a fair attempt. COST IS ACCOUNT-METERED AND ESTIMATED, NOT PER-TASK BILLED, AND ONE RATE IN IT IS A PROXY: the Genie conversations API returns no token, DBU or cost field, so nothing per-task was recorded. The figure is derived from system.billing.usage for 2026-09-18, the day all three runs ran. Databricks meters Genie with enough metadata to attribute it exactly, which is why this is a tighter attribution than a day-total: rows carry usage_metadata.genie.{surface,channel,agent_id}, so only surface=GENIE_AGENTS, channel=API against THIS space id is counted. That isolates the harness from the operator's own browser use of the same space (1.8 DBU on channel=UI, excluded) and from an unrelated GENIE_CODE session (0.018 DBU, excluded). Over 09:00-14:00Z, the block containing all 447 single-turn task-runs, the account metered 1,050.835 DBU of Genie inference plus 51.674 DBU on serverless SQL warehouse cde965bb67bf5af3 -- the warehouse the space serves from, so that is Genie executing its own queries against 58.5M rows. 1,102.509 DBU over 447 task-runs at $0.70/DBU gives $1.7265 per task and $2.3893 per correct answer (323 of 447 runs correct). Inference is 95.3% of it. Three caveats, and the first is the one that matters. (1) THE RATE IS A PROXY AND THE ACTUAL BILL WAS ZERO: the SKU is GENIE_FREE_USAGE, which has NO row in system.billing.list_prices because Genie was not charged for on this account during the run. $0.70/DBU is the Premium serverless SQL compute rate this workspace does pay, confirmed in list_prices, and is used because Databricks meters Genie consumption in serverless SQL DBUs. Read $1.7265 as what this run would cost at that rate, not as an invoice. If Genie is priced differently when the free tier ends, rescale linearly: the DBU counts above are measured and only the multiplier is assumed. (2) SMOKE TESTS ARE EXCLUDED, AND THE MULTI-TURN TAIL IS NOT YET SETTLED: the 58.1 DBU spent on smoke and cross-tier validation before 09:00Z is left out as setup, and the 123 multi-turn task-runs from 14:00-16:38Z had not landed in system.billing.usage at query time (billing lags roughly three hours), so the denominator is the 447 single-turn task-runs. This assumes a multi-turn turn costs about what a single-turn task costs. Snowflake's figure is over 447 task-runs for the same reason, so the two are directly comparable. (3) NOT THE SAME METER AS OTHER ROWS: Vanna and LangChain are billed per token by OpenAI, Claude Code's figure is API-equivalent rather than billed, Snowflake's is credit-metered, and this one is DBU-metered at a proxy rate. Four meters in one column; compare within a band, not across. One structural difference from the Snowflake row is worth naming: that row's warehouse credits cover only the reference re-execution, because Analyst is SQL-track. This row is answer-track, so Genie ran every query itself on the full dataset and that compute is inside the number. Tokens are not reported because Databricks does not meter Genie per token.
